4. **§13 Resolution column**: Table header `| ID | Question | Closes before | Resolution |` is present. All closed items carry resolution text; U-21-d, U-21-f, U-21-i carry "OPEN". ✓

**New R4 finding**: The R3 fix added the try/except but its exception clause is too narrow — `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` and `FileNotFoundError` escape, causing a full snapshot crash rather than graceful degradation when git times out or is absent.

findings.claim: The try/except in _build_snapshot that guards signing-keys parse catches only RuntimeError; subprocess.TimeoutExpired and OSError (e.g. FileNotFoundError when git binary is absent) escape the clause and crash the entire snapshot build, defeating the degradation mechanism for git-subprocess failure modes.
findings.evidence: resources.py:581 — `except RuntimeError as error:`. _git_stdout (resources.py:105-117) calls subprocess.run(..., timeout=_RESOURCE_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) where _RESOURCE_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30. subprocess.run raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired when the timeout fires; TimeoutExpired inherits from SubprocessError→Exception, not RuntimeError. FileNotFoundError (OSError) is raised when git is not on PATH. Both exceptions propagate through _read_committed_text back to _build_snapshot, escape the except clause, and unwind snapshot() to its caller. test_signing_keys_outage.py covers only the malformed-keyring (RuntimeError) and empty-keyring (RuntimeError) paths; no test exercises subprocess.TimeoutExpired or FileNotFoundError degradation.
findings.impact: Under git I/O contention, lockfile saturation, or a 30-second network partition on an HTTP git remote, _build_snapshot raises unhandled, snapshot() propagates the exception, and every MCP resource handler (scp://rules/registry, scp://decisions, scp://findings/open etc.) returns an error to the client. The intended safety net — build and serve a snapshot with key_id=null so consumers observe signing-key unavailability but still receive all other resources — is bypassed entirely. A low-privilege actor who can stall git I/O for 30 seconds (e.g. by triggering a large gc --auto, acquiring a git lockfile, or disrupting an HTTP remote for a repos-over-network deployment) can make the full SCP MCP surface unavailable rather than merely degraded. This compounds under the 021H HTTP transport because network-partition conditions are more common there.
findings.mitigation: Broaden the except clause to catch the full subprocess-failure surface: `except (RuntimeError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as error:` (or `except Exception as error:` with a narrower re-raise for truly unexpected types). Add a test in test_signing_keys_outage.py that monkey-patches subprocess.run to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired and asserts the snapshot degrades (key_id is None, error field is populated, remaining static resources are still served). The degraded payload path (_degraded_signing_keys_payload) already exists and requires no changes — only the exception clause needs widening.

self_reported_concerns: SB-R4-MAJ-001 severity calibration: MAJ rather than CRIT because (a) the git-timeout vector requires either physical access to the server filesystem or a network partition affecting an HTTP remote, both of which are operational rather than purely code-level attacks; (b) the failure mode is full-service unavailability (DoS), not a signing-key substitution or receipt-bypass; (c) the 021H HTTP transport is not yet shipped so the network-partition vector does not yet apply. If 021H ships before this finding is closed, the severity should be re-evaluated as CRIT.

Outage tests (test_signing_keys_outage.py) pass against the current RuntimeError degradation paths and correctly assert key_id=None, error field population, and propagation to all static resource URIs and per-ID handlers. They are valid regression tests for the RuntimeError surface; the gap is limited to the subprocess-exception surface described in SB-R4-MAJ-001.

R1 findings SB-MAJ-001 through SB-nit-008 closure status was verified by static analysis of the current resources.py and tools.py; no re-opened regressions were found. The snapshot lock (threading.Lock at resources.py:453) guards the check-and-build correctly with double-checked locking at lines 470-474. The stale-snapshot race noted in the prior analysis (HEAD read before lock, newer snapshot overwritten by older build) is a pre-existing bounded TOCTOU whose impact is limited to brief staleness and does not threaten signing-key integrity; it is not a new R4 finding.

I did not execute the test suite. All findings are based on static code analysis. The subprocess.TimeoutExpired exception hierarchy was verified against Python stdlib documentation (subprocess.TimeoutExpired inherits from SubprocessError which inherits from Exception, not RuntimeError).
structured_review.summary: Five R3 MAJ closures verified. Four are confirmed shut: (1) server.py instructions accurately reflects all 7 registered tools and 11 URI types; (2) trust_model.adopter_requirement carries no 'or a pinned sha256' clause; (3) §13 unknowns table carries a Resolution column with appropriate OPEN/CLOSED entries for all nine unknowns; (4) both outage regression tests exercise the RuntimeError degradation path and pass. One R3 MAJ is only partially closed: the try/except block around the signing-keys parse at _build_snapshot:564-583 exists and correctly catches RuntimeError from _parse_signing_keys, but subprocess.TimeoutExpired (raised when git hangs past the 30-second wall-clock ceiling) is a SubprocessError→Exception subtype and escapes the except RuntimeError clause entirely. When that escape occurs, _build_snapshot raises unhandled, snapshot() propagates the exception, and every in-flight MCP resource request returns an error — all resources are unavailable rather than the intended degraded state (null key_id, resources still served). The degradation invariant is bypassed for the git-timeout failure mode. No new CRIT findings. No regression on any previously closed R1/R2 finding detected: path-traversal protection via _resolve_repo_relative_path is in place and correctly rejects container-escaping paths; threading.Lock guards snapshot check-and-build; raw_text is absent from the signing-keys response; waivers.json is loaded once; prior_keys list comprehension uses current_key_id rather than the dead None-branch.
